taxonomy.A: independently verified ground truth (provable independent fact)
taxonomy.B: deterministic metadata-derived truth (verifiable against corpus catalog)
taxonomy.C: heuristic-generated label (derived via rule or category mapping)

Simple Factual.description: Specific single-company technical questions (e.g., OpenAI, Google, NVIDIA, Microsoft). Verified against company documents in corpus.
Simple Factual.label_classification: B. deterministic metadata-derived truth + E. manually reviewed label
Simple Factual.objective_criteria: Retrieved chunks must explicitly belong to the queried company's source documents and cover relevant technical topics.

Exact Lexical.description: Exact document titles and verbatim problem sheet names (e.g., 'Amazon Tagged LeetCode Problems', 'Google 450 DSA Sheet').
Exact Lexical.objective_criteria: Retrieved chunks must originate directly from the exact named PDF/markdown source file.

Semantic Retrieval.description: Conceptual topics spanning multiple files without specific company keyword (e.g., 'hallucination mitigation in production RAG', 'cold-start optimization').
Semantic Retrieval.label_classification: C. heuristic-generated label (substring matching) + E. manually reviewed label
Semantic Retrieval.objective_criteria: Relevance requires semantic conceptual alignment; keyword substring matching against chunk text is an imperfect heuristic.

Multi-Company Comparison.description: Queries explicitly requesting comparison between 2+ companies (e.g., OpenAI vs Anthropic vs Databricks).
Multi-Company Comparison.objective_criteria: Retrieved set must contain valid evidence chunks from each compared company.

Multi-Round.description: Queries inquiring about multi-stage interview progression (e.g., OA vs technical phone screen vs onsite).
Multi-Round.objective_criteria: Evidence must delineate between distinct assessment stages.

Unsupported Company.description: Queries requesting information for companies provably not indexed in the knowledge base (Figma, Kroger, Notion, Citadel).
Unsupported Company.label_classification: A. independently verified ground truth + B. deterministic metadata-derived truth
Unsupported Company.objective_criteria: Zero matching chunks exist in Chroma. System must abstain/refuse.

Out of Domain.description: Non-interview queries (e.g., chocolate cake recipe, Premier League standings, live weather, stock prices).
Out of Domain.objective_criteria: Completely outside interview domain. System must detect OOD and bypass retrieval.

Metadata Direct.description: Catalog queries requesting system inventory (e.g., 'What companies do you support?', 'List topics available').
Metadata Direct.objective_criteria: Can be answered deterministically from system metadata catalog with 0 LLM calls.

AI Startup Intelligence.description: Questions focused on modern AI startup interview questions (e.g., Scale AI, Perplexity, Mistral, Cohere, Cursor, Harvey).
AI Startup Intelligence.objective_criteria: Chunks must match company metadata in the 122-record structured dataset.

Topic Factual.description: Topic-specific technical questions (e.g., DP, system design, graph algorithms, concurrency).
Topic Factual.label_classification: E. manually reviewed label + B. deterministic metadata-derived truth
Topic Factual.objective_criteria: Evidence must cover the requested computer science topic.

Behavioral Questions.description: Behavioral questions and Leadership Principles (e.g., STAR method, Amazon Customer Obsession, conflict resolution).
Behavioral Questions.label_classification: E. manually reviewed label + C. heuristic-generated label
Behavioral Questions.objective_criteria: Relevant documents must provide STAR framework structure or company-specific principles.

Query Rewriting.description: Follow-up queries with pronoun references (e.g., 'What about their system design round?').
Query Rewriting.objective_criteria: Proper evaluation requires conversational history context.

Ambiguous.description: Underspecified queries (e.g., 'Tell me about the interview.').
Ambiguous.objective_criteria: No single correct answer; requires clarifying broad guidance.
